scope: Aggregate results only. No transactions, amounts, merchants, dates, or per-row predictions appear here. Real financial ingestion is disabled in public demo mode by design.

method.why_not_a_test_set: Earlier results informed later prompt design, so these rows have already influenced decisions. Calling them a held-out test set would claim more than they can support.
method.split: merchant-disjoint, assigned by salted hash rather than shuffled
method.where_changes_are_chosen: The development split. v3 was designed entirely from 265 development rows and measured once on the benchmark afterwards, which is the separation v2 did not respect.
method.ambiguity_policy: A row is ambiguous only when a human authored an acceptable-label set and wrote down why. Annotator disagreement is never read as ambiguity: disagreement usually means one annotator was wrong, and treating it as legitimate would inflate every system's score. No row in this benchmark carries an authored set, so acceptable-label accuracy and exact-match accuracy coincide here.

prompt_iterations.chosen_on: the benchmark itself, which was the mistake
prompt_iterations.hypothesis: LIVING_OTHER was absorbing rows that belonged elsewhere - predicted 18 times against a true support of 1. Naming it a last resort should reduce that.
prompt_iterations.change: One rule added. Five lines, none removed.
prompt_iterations.result: LIVING_OTHER F1 did not move at all: 0.1053 before and after. Accuracy, weighted F1, cost, and tail latency all worsened. Macro F1 rose only because the denominator shrank.

prompt_iterations.chosen_on: the development split, with the benchmark untouched
prompt_iterations.hypothesis: Two failures found on development under v1. REFUND scored F1 0.0000 on 19 rows - the model identified the merchant and never noticed the money had come back. TRANSFER lost 13 of 26 rows to LIVING_CARD_FEE, because nothing distinguished paying a card balance from being charged a membership fee.
prompt_iterations.change: Two rules added to v1, not to the rejected v2. Eight lines, none removed. Both were checked against development gold before being written: card payments are TRANSFER 7/7, inbound person-to-person credits are REFUND 8/8, no counterexamples.
prompt_iterations.why: Every headline accuracy metric moved up together - macro F1, weighted F1, and plain accuracy - and mean and p95 latency both fell, for 7.4% more cost per row. That is the pattern v2 failed to produce: v2 moved one metric and worsened the rest. Half the macro gain is a smaller denominator rather than better answers, which is why it is decomposed below and why the decision does not rest on macro F1.

development_did_not_predict_the_benchmar.finding: The fix that transformed the development split barely moved the benchmark, and moved it through a different category.
development_did_not_predict_the_benchmar.why: REFUND was already at F1 0.6667 on the benchmark under v1, against 0.0000 on development, so the failure the rule was written for did not exist there. The benchmark's gain came mostly from LIVING_CARD_FEE, 0.0000 to 0.5000. Merchant-disjoint splitting produces genuinely different difficulty on each side, and this is what that looks like when measured rather than assumed.
development_did_not_predict_the_benchmar.reading: The development number is what tuning buys. The benchmark number is what generalises. Reporting the first as the result is how benchmarks stop meaning anything.

failure_modes.name: confident_but_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: The model was sure and wrong. The failure a reviewer would not think to check, and the one that most needs the confidence signal to mean something.

failure_modes.name: abstention_would_have_been_better
failure_modes.what_it_means: The model was already unsure and answered anyway. Abstaining would have cost coverage and saved an error, which is the trade the routing threshold exists to make.

failure_modes.name: rules_right_model_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: The deterministic baseline got these and the model did not. Every row here is an argument for the hybrid, and against replacing the rules with the model.

failure_modes.name: model_right_rules_wrong
failure_modes.what_it_means: What the model is actually buying: rows the baseline could not answer or answered wrongly. Counted over correct model rows, not failures.

failure_modes.name: thin_description
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on rows whose description is under 15 characters. Not a prompt problem: the row does not carry enough to decide, and a better prompt cannot add context that is absent.

failure_modes.name: polysemous_merchant
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on a merchant that carries more than one gold label in this dataset. Genuinely two things; no description-only system resolves these reliably.

failure_modes.name: annotators_disagreed_too
failure_modes.what_it_means: Wrong on rows where the two human annotators also disagreed. The model is failing where people find it hard, which bounds how much of this is fixable by prompting.

failure_modes.name: abstained
failure_modes.what_it_means: Declined to answer. Not an error, but it is lost coverage and it belongs in the same picture.

failure_analysis.note: Counts and taxonomy label pairs only. No merchant, amount, date, or transaction appears here or can be recovered from it.

limitations: One model, one provider. No second vendor has been scored on this benchmark, so nothing here says how hard the task is in general.
135 benchmark rows. Five categories carry fewer than five rows each, so one corrected row moves macro F1 by several points.
Single runs, no repeats. Run-to-run variance is not separated from the effect of a prompt, though the v1 benchmark reproduced to four decimal places across two runs a day apart.
No authored-ambiguous rows, so the ambiguous stratum is structurally present and empty, and acceptable-label accuracy equals exact match.
One annotator, adjudicating their own double pass. Inter-annotator agreement is measured but not independent.
backlog: Routing on confidence. 20 benchmark rows were answered below 0.60 and wrong, nearly all collapsing into LIVING_OTHER; mean confidence is 0.84 when right and 0.61 when wrong, so the signal is informative enough to abstain on.
LIVING_TRAVEL against COMMUTE_TRANSIT_FARE remains the largest confusion, and 5 of those rows have descriptions under 15 characters, which no prompt can fix.
An OpenAI adapter, to score a second vendor on this same frozen benchmark with labels, split, and scoring unchanged.
